mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate for equity valuation, increasing present value of future cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship holds consistently across monetary policy regimes.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS levels below 2.5% correlate with negative 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 50% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.5 percentage points within 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and stagnant monetary policy (FEDFUNDS) signals an impending tightening cycle, increasing real interest rates and depressing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The CPIAUCSL-FEDFUNDS interaction fails to predict returns when correlation with 20-day SPX returns is below 0.05 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth (INDPRO above 115) indicates robust supply chain conditions, boosting corporate output and margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days during expansionary phases.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth above 115 fails to produce positive 60-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1000 thousand units within 2 months signals weak consumer demand, reducing retail activity and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls > 5% in 2 months, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher employment growth (PAYEMS) relative to historical averages increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth above 100 thousand units per month correlates with negative 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 50% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint behavior of strong employment growth (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) signals a robust labor market, boosting consumer confidence and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The PAYEMS-UNRATE interaction fails to predict positive 5-day returns when correlation with SPX returns is below 0.05 in a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.0% signals a monetary tightening cycle, raising real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.
